To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the number of recommendations received by users is a significant determinant of their overall satisfaction with the recommender system, (b) the number of ratings that a user makes is a significant determinant for the number of recommendations that the user will receive in the future, (c) users who are not satisfied with the recommender systems will make fewer ratings in the future, and (d) users are not willing to rate more than 10 items in a single day.

(1) the most important factors in the choice of a recommender system are its accuracy and its speed of response, (2) a system that uses the most accurate recommender algorithms will not necessarily be the most useful, because of the tradeoffs in accuracy versus speed, and (3) the accuracy of the recommender algorithms can be improved by using more data, but the speed of response can be improved by reducing the amount of data.

(1) the most important factor in the choice of a new car is the brand, and (2) the most important factors in the choice of an apartment are location and price, and (3) the most important decision factor in the choice between a new car and a used car is price.
